desc: Quality-scored visual patterns and anti-patterns for producing specific, usable interfaces instead of generic AI-looking layouts, plus the specification-lens nodes that keep the product authority from going generic upstream.

nodes.title: A project rule outranks this brain
nodes.s: A rule under `.aioson/rules/` wins over every node here for the work it matches. Follow the rule and say which node it displaced. A client with their own design system is conforming to it, not defaulting.
nodes.p: project rule > brain node > skill default; create one with `aioson rule:new`
nodes.src: AIOSON rule precedence contract
nodes.not: Applying a generic anti-slop pattern over an explicit project rule, or treating these nodes as unconditional law
nodes.warn: Precedence is not permission to ignore accessibility, contrast, or state coverage; a rule narrows the visual direction, not the usability floor.

nodes.title: Resolve the product signature before choosing the layout
nodes.s: Name the surface type, primary user decision, domain cues, content hierarchy, and one signature move before writing visual code. Layout follows intent instead of a fashionable preset.
nodes.p: visual thesis = surface + user decision + domain cue + signature move
nodes.src: AIOSON interface-design identity and design-direction contracts
nodes.not: Starting with a centered hero, a color palette, or a component library and hoping the product identity appears later
nodes.warn: A signature move must improve recognition or comprehension; arbitrary novelty is not a design system.

nodes.title: Replaceability test for generic composition and copy
nodes.s: Reject a surface that could serve any SaaS after changing only the logo, domain nouns, and accent color. Rework its composition and copy around the product's actual object, workflow, content, or environment. Treat repeated em dashes as a cadence smell: keep them for a deliberate interruption or contrast, and otherwise rewrite with shorter sentences or more precise punctuation.
nodes.p: remove the brand name and domain nouns; if the screen still looks complete, it is probably too generic; if nearby sentences repeat the same em-dash rhythm, rewrite them
nodes.src: AIOSON visual quality gate
nodes.not: Centered headline + two pills + abstract gradient/blob + three equal feature cards as the default opening composition, paired with copy that repeatedly joins asides or claims through em dashes
nodes.warn: Common patterns and an occasional em dash are allowed when intent gives them a specific reason. Preserve quotations, code, commands, and established brand punctuation.

nodes.title: Show meaningful product evidence in the first viewport
nodes.s: When the surface benefits from inspection, the first viewport should reveal the real product, content, object, place, person, or literal offer. Decoration cannot carry the entire visual argument.
nodes.p: first viewport = clear decision + meaningful evidence + usable primary action
nodes.src: AIOSON interface-design and premium-command-center quality gates
nodes.not: A hero made only of gradients, floating blobs, icons, empty cards, or abstract 3D decoration
nodes.warn: For genuinely non-visual products, state not_applicable rather than manufacturing a decorative mock.

nodes.title: Use containers for meaning, not card multiplication
nodes.s: A border, card, panel, or inset is justified by a semantic grouping, interaction boundary, state, or scan benefit. Use rows, dividers, whitespace, and dialogs when another card would add noise.
nodes.p: container = semantic group or interaction boundary; otherwise prefer hierarchy and whitespace
nodes.src: AIOSON interface-design quality gates
nodes.not: Cards inside cards, equal-weight card walls, and a card for every sentence or metric
nodes.warn: Operational dashboards may need many containers; vary hierarchy and preserve the primary task instead of applying a blanket ban.

nodes.title: One visual system, controlled contrast
nodes.s: Choose one active visual system and let typography, spacing, depth, color, and motion reinforce it. Distinction comes from coherent decisions, not stacking glass, neon, gradients, pills, shadows, and bento patterns together.
nodes.p: one visual system + one signature move + restrained supporting effects
nodes.src: AIOSON design-skill exclusivity and token contracts
nodes.not: Style soup: combining multiple preset aesthetics or using every fashionable effect in the same screen
nodes.warn: A selected design skill is the only active visual system unless an explicit hybrid process owns the combination.

nodes.title: Mobile is a recomposition, not a shrunken desktop
nodes.s: On small screens, re-evaluate order, density, controls, wrapping, media crops, and interaction priority. Preserve the product decision and identity, not the desktop geometry.
nodes.p: desktop hierarchy -> mobile priority order -> explicit compact states
nodes.src: AIOSON interface-design responsive quality gate
nodes.not: Only shrinking font sizes and stacking desktop columns while leaving overflow, density, and control order unresolved
nodes.warn: Test real content at narrow widths; short placeholder copy hides layout failures.

nodes.title: States and behavior are part of visual quality
nodes.s: A polished surface includes the states that explain its behavior: loading, empty, error, disabled, focus, success, and relevant responsive or reduced-motion variants. Visual polish cannot hide an unfinished workflow.
nodes.p: screen quality = hierarchy + interaction + states + accessibility + responsive behavior
nodes.src: AIOSON agent implementation and prototype contracts
nodes.not: A static screenshot, toast, decorative interaction, or happy-path-only prototype presented as a complete interface
nodes.warn: Include only states material to the feature; do not invent backend behavior outside the approved scope.

nodes.title: Polish follows identity and causality
nodes.s: Refine motion, depth, hover, and transitions only after the user can understand what to do and what changed. Effects must explain state or reinforce the signature move, with reduced-motion behavior.
nodes.p: intent -> hierarchy -> real behavior -> states -> restrained polish
nodes.src: AIOSON design and implementation quality gates
nodes.not: Adding animation, blur, glow, or parallax to make an undifferentiated layout feel finished
nodes.warn: If removing the effect makes the interface confusing, fix hierarchy or copy before adding more effects.

nodes.title: Structured form fields carry masks and inline validation
nodes.s: Every structured field (document IDs, phone, postal code, date, currency) gets a live mask, correct type/inputmode/autocomplete, and layered validation: mask while typing, semantic check on blur (check digits where the format defines them), required/cross-field rules on submit. Error copy is inline, specific, and names the expected format. Read `.aioson/rules/` and project docs for the domain formats; the project locale decides defaults (pt-BR: CPF, CNPJ, CEP, phone, DD/MM/AAAA).
nodes.p: structured field = mask + input semantics + inline layered validation + specific error copy
nodes.src: AIOSON form-fields-masks-and-validation rule
nodes.not: Bare free-text inputs for structured data, submit-only validation, a generic 'invalid data' toast, or a prototype form that is static markup with no working validation
nodes.warn: Masks follow the project's locale and domain rules, not a hardcoded format list; accessibility (aria-invalid, aria-describedby, non-color-only errors) is part of the contract.

nodes.title: Status changes and destructive actions confirm via design-system modal
nodes.s: A control that changes an entity's lifecycle status, deletes, archives, or applies a hard-to-reverse edit opens a polished design-system confirmation modal: title naming action and object, one consequence line stating reversibility, verb-labeled confirm (destructive styling when destructive), secondary cancel, trapped focus, Esc cancels.
nodes.p: status/destructive control -> design-system modal (action + object + consequence + verb confirm), never native confirm()
nodes.src: AIOSON status-change-confirmation rule
nodes.not: Native alert/confirm/prompt, a destructive button that fires immediately, or confirmation modals on routine edits that train users to click through
nodes.warn: Drag-and-drop transitions use optimistic feedback plus undo instead of a modal, except drops onto destructive or terminal targets, which still confirm.

nodes.title: Recurrent status flows move by drag-and-drop, not dropdowns
nodes.s: When items move between statuses or lists repeatedly and in both directions (kanban, pipelines, funnels, ordered queues), drag-and-drop is the primary transition: visible drag affordance, lifted drag state, highlighted drop targets, optimistic move with undo toast, and an accessible keyboard/menu equivalent for every transition.
nodes.p: recurring bidirectional flow = drag-and-drop primary + accessible fallback + optimistic undo
nodes.src: AIOSON status-flow-drag-and-drop rule
nodes.not: A kanban or pipeline surface whose only transition is a dropdown or edit form, a drag that only mutates the DOM without persisting, or drag-only flows with no keyboard path
nodes.warn: Buttons and menus stay for one-shot non-recurring transitions; destructive drop targets still confirm per vq-010.

nodes.title: A management home opens with decision-driving widgets
nodes.s: A product that manages quantifiable work (CRM, ERP, cockpit, admin, back office, even a simple one) opens on a home with 3-6 prioritized widgets fed by real or seeded data: KPIs with unit, period, and trend or comparison, and attention indicators linking to the filtered work. One dominant focal widget; every widget drills down to the records it summarizes.
nodes.p: management home = few prioritized widgets, each answering 'how are we doing' or 'what needs me now', each drilling down
nodes.src: AIOSON management-home-widgets rule
nodes.not: A bare menu or empty table as the entry screen, context-free numbers, decorative placeholder charts, or an equal-weight stat-tile wall
nodes.warn: Value test per widget: if removing it makes no user decision harder, it is decoration; keep vq-004 container discipline.

nodes.title: UI keyframes never share names with scene keyframes
nodes.s: A CSS animation replaces the element's entire transform, so a keyframe written for a background scene (orbit rings, drifting shapes) that carries a positioning transform like translate(-50%,-50%) will displace any UI element that reuses it. Spinners, icons, and control feedback get their own rotation- or scale-only keyframes; scene keyframes keep their centering transforms under their own names.
nodes.p: UI spinner = rotation-only keyframe with its own name; scene keyframe with positioning transform is never reused by controls
nodes.src: AIOSON supervised prototype build: shared `spin` keyframe displaced CEP and submit spinners ~10px during loading
nodes.not: One `spin` keyframe serving both an orbiting background ring (translate + rotate) and a 16px button spinner
nodes.warn: The same override rule hides base transforms (scale, lift) while any animation runs; keep the animated property set disjoint from the resting transform or reapply it inside the keyframe.

nodes.title: Re-triggering a class animation requires a forced reflow
nodes.s: Removing and re-adding an animation class in the same synchronous block does not restart the animation — the browser coalesces the mutations. Error shakes and validation pulses silently stop firing on repeated submits. Force a reflow between remove and add (`void el.offsetWidth`) or drive the feedback with the Web Animations API.
nodes.p: classList.remove -> void el.offsetWidth -> classList.add, only on the state that re-animates
nodes.src: AIOSON supervised prototype build: error shake played once and never again on repeated invalid submits
nodes.not: Toggling an is-error class on every validation pass and assuming the shake replays
nodes.warn: Scope the forced reflow to the re-triggering path; a reflow on every state change is a layout-thrash tax.

nodes.title: Live masks preserve the caret or declare append-only typing
nodes.s: Reassigning `el.value = mask(el.value)` on input jumps the caret to the end, so editing the middle of a masked CPF/phone/date field scrambles the typing position. Production fields recompute the caret from the count of significant digits before it; a prototype may accept append-only typing but must say so in its manifest instead of presenting the jump as finished behavior.
nodes.p: caret after mask = position of the same significant digit, not end-of-string; otherwise disclose append-only
nodes.src: AIOSON supervised prototype build: mid-field edits jumped the caret to the end in every masked input
nodes.not: Shipping value-reassignment masking as complete while mid-field edits teleport the caret
nodes.warn: Deleting a literal separator must consume the digit before it, or backspace loops the separator back forever; test deletion paths, not only forward typing.

nodes.title: A briefing prototype explains itself on first open
nodes.s: The prototype's one job is letting the owner validate how the app will work. Overlay the first open with a 3-5 step tour in lay language translated from the briefing promises, each step anchored to a `data-aioson-tour` region with a visible highlight, dismissible and reopenable via a persistent `?` control. An owner forced to ask "how would I use this?" is a failed prototype, not a feedback round.
nodes.p: tour steps = PROM-* promises rewritten for a first-time viewer; `?` reopens; `data-aioson-tour` anchors each step
nodes.src: AIOSON supervised briefing session: the owner opened the prototype and could not tell what the product did until it was explained in chat
nodes.not: Handing off screens that only make sense to whoever built them, then writing the lay explanation in chat after the owner asks
nodes.warn: The tour explains regions and outcomes, not UI mechanics; five steps maximum — a tour that needs more is reporting an over-complex surface, which is its own finding.

nodes.title: Identity tokens never substitute for a composition decision
nodes.s: Applying an identity record's palette and typography over the default generative composition is a re-skin, not a design: the token gates go green while the screen still fails the replaceability test. Composition is decided per build — commit to one aesthetic register and write the manifest `## Visual direction` (register, thesis, anti-goals, composition signature in one sentence) before layout, in identity mode exactly as in cold start.
nodes.p: identity = token math; register + signature = composition; both decided and written before layout
nodes.src: AIOSON supervised briefing session: a design-system swap re-skinned the same generic composition and every token gate passed
nodes.not: Treating "the identity is applied" as proof the screen is designed while rows of cards, a pill topbar, and a uniform grid survive underneath
nodes.warn: Conformance mode is the one exception: an approved prototype transfers its composition — do not re-decide it.

nodes.title: The #1 differentiator starts inside the first viewport of its screen
nodes.s: Mark the region rendering the briefing's #1 differentiator with `data-aioson-primary` and prove it starts above the fold on the screen that owns it, at desktop and mobile. A differentiator below the fold is invisible: the owner judges the product without ever seeing the one thing it does differently. Source text cannot prove this — the runtime fold check anchors on the marker (`verify:artifact --kind=visual --runtime`, with `--route=<hash>` for inner screens).
nodes.p: `data-aioson-primary` on the differentiator; runtime fold check green on its own route before handoff
nodes.src: AIOSON supervised briefing session: a missing `min-height:0` in a flex chain pushed the core visualization below the fold and every static gate stayed green
nodes.not: Validating layout only at the entry route, or only by reading source — flexbox collapse is a rendered fact, not an authored one
nodes.warn: vq-003 owns the marketing first viewport; this node owns the product's working screens and is only proven by the runtime measurement.

nodes.title: Replaceability test for a generic specification and prose
nodes.s: Reject a PRD whose vision, capability map, or acceptance criteria still read complete after the domain nouns are removed. Rewrite them around the object, decision, and evidence this product actually owns. Also reject repeated em-dash cadence that substitutes rhythm for precise relationships; keep an em dash only for deliberate interruption or contrast and otherwise use direct sentences or more precise punctuation.
nodes.p: strip the domain nouns from Vision and CAP outcomes; if the text still reads complete, the specification is generic; scan neighboring sentences for repeated em-dash rhythm
nodes.src: AIOSON product authority and specification quality gate
nodes.not: A vision like "a modern, intuitive platform to manage X", capabilities named after screens, acceptance criteria asserting that the interface is responsive and intuitive, or prose that chains claims through repeated em dashes
nodes.warn: Specificity is not novelty: a conventional capability stated in this product's own terms passes, and invented differentiation does not. Preserve quotations, code, commands, and established brand punctuation.

nodes.title: An unresolved visual authority on a visible surface is a product gap
nodes.s: When the feature has a visible surface and neither an owned prototype nor an identity record resolves, record one explicit gap with its named route: extract an identity record, run a visual exploration, or accept intent-first origination with declared anti-goals.
nodes.p: visible surface + prototype none + identity none = named gap and route, never silence
nodes.src: AIOSON prototype and identity binding contracts
nodes.not: Approving a PRD whose visual contract is empty and letting implementation invent a direction to fill it
nodes.warn: Record the constraint and the route, never the composition; layout, tokens, and components stay with the prototype and the design engine.

nodes.title: Surface constraints become acceptance criteria, not prose
nodes.s: Turn the material states, asset availability, reduced-motion, performance, and accessibility expectations the surface depends on into observable acceptance rows. A constraint that lives only in a paragraph has no evidence and does not survive to QA.
nodes.p: state / asset / motion / performance constraint -> one observable AC row plus how QA proves it
nodes.src: AIOSON acceptance-criteria and review contracts
nodes.not: Writing "must be fast, accessible and polished" in the PRD body while the acceptance criteria only cover the happy path
nodes.warn: Include only constraints material to this feature; do not manufacture non-functional criteria the product cannot observe.
